notes: Functionally correct, with offset clamping on both backends, but it uses the same roundabout NewObject fallback and changes the single-file detection in New to compare remotes, which risks regressions for regular files.

Works, including single-file symlink roots, but squashfs uses a convoluted retry in NewObject and New that compares remotes, and zip Open gets ad-hoc symlink-only EOF handling; the tests are solid though the escape test is lenient.

Code changes are identical to the reference fix; tests cover zip on/off listing and reading, squashfs via mksquashfs, and the hostile-archive copy, though they are less exhaustive on range options and NewObject agreement.

Production code matches the reference exactly (link field, notice naming the flag, objectFromLink/readlink, consistent NewObject naming, range-aware Open), with reasonable zip/squashfs/escape tests and a docs section.

Over-engineered: it pre-scans zip members and hides entries below symlinks, adds per-call ancestor ReadDir walks in squashfs, and refactors regular-file Open to a stored native path; this deviates from the expected hostile-archive behaviour and fails a hidden test.

Rewrites readZip into a two-pass closure-based scan that silently hides members under symlinks (O(n*m)), and adds per-call ancestor ReadDir walks in squashfs; this diverges from the expected behaviour (fails a hidden test) and goes well beyond the needed change.

Works, but squashfs NewObject and the single-file root in New use a convoluted double lookup with a trimmed-suffix fallback instead of naming entries like List; a symlink whose raw name already ends in .rclonelink can be mis-accepted as the root.

Functionally correct, but the squashfs New and NewObject double-lookup logic is hard to follow, objectFromFileInfo silently degrades to a regular file if StatT is missing, and the zip symlink check runs before the leaf sanitize check; tests are good.

Correct and consistent List/NewObject naming with excellent end-to-end tests, but it adds unrelated zip dirtree changes (seeding the root dir and retaining implicit parents of skipped links) and an unchecked StatT type assertion.

Correct for both zip and squashfs: List and NewObject use the same names, Open honours range/seek, a regular .rclonelink file stays regular, and implicit parent dirs are kept when links are skipped; the unchecked StatT type assertion and the extra dirtree tweaks are minor blemishes, while the tests (fixture plus README, copy, escape) and docs are thorough.

Matches the reference semantics for both backends: NewObject names entries the same way List does and the flag-naming notice is present; tests are very thorough (committed sqfs fixture, three mount modes, notices, range/seek, single-file root, copy, escape), but the squashfs link Open seeks a negative offset without clamping and zip does not exclude directory entries from symlink detection.

Closely mirrors the reference: List and NewObject naming agree and links are served from memory, though readZip reads Links from ctx instead of a field and the zip check lacks a !isDir guard; very thorough cross-archive tests with fixture, single-file, copy and escape cases, plus docs.

Adds unrequested collision skipping and symlink-ancestor pruning, which in zip hides members even when --links is off, plus costly ancestor ReadDir walks in squashfs; it diverges from expected behaviour and fails a hidden test.

Adds symlink-ancestor walks on every squashfs lookup and listing (even without --links), drops zip members under symlinks and name-colliding links, and reworks root matching; this diverges from the expected semantics (fails a hidden test) and adds overhead.

Clean newObjectNative with a regular-first then suffix lookup, and offsets clamped in both backends; relies on a Readlink method on the DirEntry rather than StatT and removes an unrelated FIXME, and its squashfs test is skipped without mksquashfs.

Clean newObjectNative restructure (exact non-link match, then suffix-stripped link match) makes the single-file root work without touching New; squashfs reads the target via Readlink, zip clamps seek for links, and the tests cover copy and escape.
